title: Cyberspace Warfare Development Officer (II) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DC I
raw_text:
3. MOS 1705, Cyberspace Warfare Development Officer (II) (LtCol to Capt)
PMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Cyberspace Warfare Development Officers provide cyber
warfare and capabilities development leadership for the creation,
integration, synchronization, and implementation of cyber warfare
technologies, capabilities, weapon systems, and tactics, techniques, and
procedures (TTPs) to deliver effects. They are a senior SME that leverages
their technical knowledge and operational experience to advise service and
joint force commanders, analyze and endorse requirements, and facilitate the
rapid acquisition of cyber capabilities. They analyze data, implement
development, security, operations (DevSecOps) into the software development
pipeline; and manage the development of artificial intelligence/ machine
learning (AI/ML) solutions within the joint cyber warfighting architecture
(JCWA). Cyberspace Warfare Development Officer establish enduring
interagency and intelligence community (IC) partnerships that ensure
capability interoperability and deconfliction of cyber effects.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Must be willing to submit to a counterintelligence scope
polygraph examination.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

        (4) Limited duty officers assigned this MOS must have previously
served in PMOSs 1710 or 1720. This prerequisite may be waived by the Deputy
Commandant for Information on a case-by-case basis for applicants from other
occupational fields who possesses noteworthy cyber warfare experience and a
current or previous successful tour within the US Cyber Command Cyber Mission
Force.

            (5) Security requirement:

            (a) Must meet sensitive compartmented information (SCI)
eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background T5 investigation.

            (b) Must complete SCI pre-screen interview with HQMC SSO for
assignment qualification per DoN and HQMC SCI policies and procedures.

    c. Requirements. Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as
prescribed in MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.




                                          1-84                   Enclosure (1)
 1114                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Computer and Information Systems Manager, 11-3021.

            (2) Data Scientists, 15-2051.00.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Offensive Cyberspace Warfare Officer, 1710.

            (2) Defensive Cyberspace Weapons Officer, 1720.

            (3) Cyberspace Warfare Operator, 1721.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
